title: Wabi Raises $55M at $1.25B for Its Shared Personal AI Agent
dek: Replika founder Eugenia Kuyda's new AI app is built for families and friends.

facts.label: New funding round led by IVP

caption:
The founder of Replika just turned a pivot into a billion-dollar bet 🚀

Wabi, the personal AI agent from Eugenia Kuyda, raised $55 million at a $1.25 billion valuation. IVP led the round, with Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Forerunner and the Amazon Alexa Fund joining, plus angels like Shopify's Tobi Lütke, Salesforce's Marc Benioff and Marissa Mayer.

Unlike ChatGPT-style chatbots built for one person, Wabi is made for couples, families and friends. Its AI builds shared mini-apps you keep using, like a family meal plan that becomes a grocery list or a 30-day fitness challenge with friends. It's on iOS, Android and Mac, with Windows coming soon.

At AI Parabellum we see this as a sign that the AI agent race is moving from solo chats to shared spaces. But Wabi hasn't shared user numbers yet, so treat the valuation as a bet, not proof.
